name: Scalp Relief Brush
tagline: Five minutes that undo a whole day of tension.

trend.signal: Scalp brushes named in beauty/self-care as a leading 2026 short-form category; criteria met: demonstrable in under 3 seconds, tangible problem, sits in the $20-40 impulse band.

positioning.problem: Your head feels tight before the day is even over.
positioning.agitation: You roll your shoulders, drink water, maybe take something. The tension sits higher up than any of that reaches.
positioning.solution: Silicone nodes that let you work the scalp directly — in the shower or dry, in about five minutes.
positioning.demoIn3s: Hand draws the brush slowly across a scalp; hair lifts and separates behind it.
positioning.buyer: 25-45, already spends on skincare, wants a ritual not a gadget.

benefits.title: Works wet or dry
benefits.body: In the shower with product, or on dry hair while you read.

benefits.title: Soft silicone nodes
benefits.body: Flexible tips that move over the scalp instead of dragging hair.

benefits.title: Fits your hand
benefits.body: Shaped so your wrist stays neutral through a full five minutes.

howItWorks.title: Section
howItWorks.body: Part hair loosely so the nodes reach skin, not just hair.

howItWorks.title: Work in circles
howItWorks.body: Slow, small circles. Front to crown, then crown to nape.

howItWorks.title: Rinse and dry
howItWorks.body: Warm water, shake out, air dry. No maintenance beyond that.

faq.q: Can I use it on wet hair?
faq.a: Yes — it is designed for use in the shower with shampoo or conditioner.
The nodes are rounded and flexible. Work slowly in circles rather than dragging it through tangles.

disclaimers: This is a personal care accessory, not a medical device. It is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any condition, and makes no claim to affect hair growth.
